extraction.name: AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC)
extraction.description: The ARC dataset consists of 7,787 natural, grade-school science multiple-choice questions authored for standardized tests, partitioned into a Challenge Set of 2,590 questions and an Easy Set of 5,197 questions. The paper also releases the ARC Corpus, a corpus of 14 million science-related sentences relevant to the task, along with baseline neural models and a leaderboard to encourage research in advanced question answering.
extraction.creator: Peter Clark; Isaac Cowhey; Oren Etzioni; Tushar Khot; Ashish Sabharwal; Carissa Schoenick; Oyvind Tafjord
extraction.citeAs: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, and Oyvind Tafjord. Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. arXiv:1803.05457v1, 2018.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The ARC dataset was assembled through several months of extensive search and investigation to obtain publicly releasable natural, grade-school science questions authored for standardized tests, drawn from a variety of sources. The ARC Corpus was created by using a major search engine to run a large series of automatically constructed science-related queries from hand-written templates for 80 science topics, collecting the top several documents from each search, de-duplicating them, stripping them to text, chunking them into sentences, and augmenting the corpus with the AristoMini corpus.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator; Web Scraping; Software Collection; Document analysis; Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset source data are non-diagram, multiple-choice science questions authored for standardized tests and drawn from sources such as state assessment programs and other exam providers. The ARC Corpus source data are science-related web documents retrieved via a major search engine, plus the AristoMini corpus containing dictionary definitions from Wiktionary, articles from Simple Wikipedia tagged as science, and additional science sentences collected from the Web.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The models were trained on the Science Entailment dataset, "a dataset created in a similar manner where crowdworkers annotated the premises and hypotheses as entailing or not."
extraction.rai:dataBiases: scores become dominated by the performance of simple algorithms (information retrieval, statistical correlations), which biases research towards incrementally improving those algorithms rather than exploring the larger AI challenges that the more difficult questions demand; retrieval bias of the underlying IR methods is towards sentences that are very similar to the question, and away from sentences that individually only partially match the question but together fully explain the correct answer
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Challenge Set is only an approximation of “hard” questions because it is operationally defined as questions answered incorrectly by two baseline solvers; the categorization of knowledge and reasoning types is necessarily approximate and subjective; the ARC Corpus has only approximately 75% of sampled collected documents judged as science relevant; simple retrieval methods are not able to exploit the ARC Corpus to correctly answer many questions even when relevant knowledge is present; the question-to-assertion conversion can lead to non-grammatical sentences
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is presented to encourage AI research in advanced question answering and to help the field move towards more difficult tasks requiring reasoning rather than surface-level cues alone
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: the corpus vocabulary includes a small number of proper nouns not appearing in the corpus, including names such as Daphne, Sooj, and LaKeisha
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: to encourage AI research in advanced question answering; as a challenge to the community for question answering requiring more powerful knowledge and reasoning; for training and evaluation of QA systems and baseline neural models on science question answering
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The ARC Dataset, Corpus, three baseline neural models, and the leaderboard are available from http://data.allenai.org/arc
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The Challenge Set contains questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm and a word co-occurrence algorithm, while the Easy Set contains the remainder.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The top several documents from each search were collected and de-duplicated, and then the content of these documents was stripped down to capture just the text in each document. The resulting text was then chunked into sentences.
